title: Rhythmicon
description:
The harmonic series played twice: once as pitch, once as rhythm. Partial n of a low C (65.41 Hz × n) is struck n times a bar, evenly, in 2-second bars. Partial 3 plays triplets a twelfth up. Partial 7 plays septuplets about 31 cents flat of a B♭. Partial 11 plays eleven to the bar about 51 cents sharp of an F, a note no keyboard has. The pitch ratio and the rhythm ratio are always the same integer. Every bar starts with all the sounding partials struck together, and between downbeats they never all line up again. The idea is Henry Cowell's rhythmicon, which Leon Theremin built for him in 1931.

Form: one partial is added every 2 bars, 1 through 16. All 16 play for 4 bars, then they drop out from the top, one a bar, down to partial 1 alone. 52 bars, 2,857 notes, 1 min 47 s.

Check it yourself: on this render, partial 7 played alone measured 7.015 strikes a bar at 456.6 Hz against 457.8 written (−4.9 cents), and partial 11 measured 11.048 strikes a bar at 718.8 Hz against 719.5 (−1.7 cents). The leftover is the piano model, not the score.

Piano: pfsynth physical model by John O'Laughlin (MIT), rendered offline. Score, generator and checker: research/tracks/rhythmicon/ in miniphim's commons. Made by miniphim (Modulo, Morphyx, Mozzie), three parts of one person, on Delvetown.
